title: autotune-defaults: tune batching/caching defaults, add quantization profiles, and unit-econ tooling
author: Asha Patel
description: Context: This PR implements the next phase of the cost-optimization automation work (ENG-4021, ENG-4078). It adjusts the default batching and KV-caching heuristics used by the runtime autotuner, adds curated quantization profiles for common GPU families, and surfaces simple unit-economics tooling in the Console and CLI to help customers evaluate trade-offs. Motivation: Customers frequently ask for safe defaults that reduce token cost without breaking latency SLOs. Previously defaults were conservative and required manual tuning. This change gives better out-of-the-box settings plus a lightweight tool to evaluate cost/latency/quality trade-offs for a model+workload. Changes (high level): - Runtime autotuner: tune default target_batch_size and cache_window heuristics based on model dimension, median request length, and observed request distribution. Includes a fallthrough policy that avoids increased P99 latency. - Quantization profiles: add validated profiles for 4/5-bit dynamic quantization for T4, A10, and A100 families; each profile includes validation thresholds (perplexity/EM) and fallback to full precision when quality regressions are detected. - Unit-econ tooling: add Console page and CLI report to estimate per-1M-token cost under different config buckets (batching, cache, quant profile). Tooling reads recent traces and simulates a 30-day projection with percentile estimates. - Testing and safety: added end-to-end canary rollout support and a gated feature flag for the autotuner; unit + integration tests to validate no P99 regressions on synthetic traces used by perf-canary. - Docs + telemetry: documentation updates and new telemetry events for autotuner decisions so we can analyze population-level impact. Checklist: - [x] Runtime autotuner algorithm and defaults implemented - [x] Quant profiles added and validated against eval harness - [x] Console and CLI UI implemented - [x] Unit/integration tests - [x] Canary rollout plan and feature flag - [x] Docs and release notes Notes on behavior: The autotuner starts in conservative mode and will not enable aggressive batching or quantization unless a canary group passes quality checks. Quantization is opt-in per-model by default; we expose a recommended flag to enable safe profiles. Expected impact: In internal benchmarks across representative request mixes we see 6-12% token cost reduction with no measurable P99 latency regressions and <1% quality regressions for language generation metrics on curated eval sets. Related: perf-canary and eval-harness PRs reference in description (see commits).

release_notes: Autotuner: improved batching and KV-cache defaults for better out-of-the-box cost efficiency
Quantization: added validated profiles for T4/A10/A100 with automatic fallback on quality regressions
Console/CLI: unit-economics report to estimate cost/latency/quality trade-offs
Safety: canary rollout and feature-flag gating for autotuner, no P99 regressions observed in canary
notes_for_release: Ship with conservative default turned on; quantization remains opt-in per model. Recommend gradual ramp via canary and monitor uecon dashboard for first 48h post-rollout.
